content:
This week saw contradictory reports about whether Apple has abandoned plans to launch an all-new iPhone design next year, which I'm tentatively calling the iPhone 20 Pro.

An Apple analyst claimed the company found the task too challenging, but Bloomberg was quick to clarify that this isn't the case, and that the design will launch as planned in 2027. And today there's new evidence supporting the latter view...

Contradictory reports

Apple's former design chief Jony Ive has often spoken of his long-term vision of turning the iPhone into a sheet of glass, and the company believes it will continue to pursue this direction even after his departure.

We've previously seen conflicting reports about what this new device might be called. Some say it will have a standalone name, like the iPhone X and the upcoming iPhone Ultra (possibly). Others say it will simply be next year's Pro model, so it will be called the iPhone 19 Pro. Still others say Apple will skip a generation to mark the 20th anniversary of the device's launch, calling it the iPhone 20 Pro.

This week's events saw further developments, with an analyst at Jefferies claiming Apple had shelved the project, but Bloomberg's Mark Gurman said that wasn't the case. I've previously shared my own thoughts on what might actually be happening.

iPhone 20 Pro appears in the supply chain

Chinese leaker Digital Chat Station (DCS) has now joined the fray, saying the device's display has appeared in Apple's supply chain, and matches what we expected it to look like.

We expect Apple to use a more sophisticated version, like the visual illusion effect on the Apple Watch display, to create the impression of a screen wrapping around the edges of the device. Another leaker, Ice Universe, described it this way:

DCS used very similar wording to describe what they saw in the supply chain.

This largely supports my own view: while next year's design is not the endpoint of the journey toward the single sheet of glass vision, it will be a significant step in that direction.
